slice.topic: Database join cardinality bounds as an entropy/polymatroid toolkit for partially observed nested symbolic constraints
slice.repository_context: The role-local cross_field directory was enumerated at S_commit to reconstruct continuation; no authoritative LATEST/STATE continuation was recovered from that bounded listing, so the role rule permitting the highest-value non-conflicting path was used. No prior repository artifact was used as substantive evidence for the mathematical conclusions below.

source_lineage.source: Uotila and Lu, Quantum Information-Theoretical Size Bounds for Conjunctive Queries with Functional Dependencies
source_lineage.outcome: The abstract explicitly connects conjunctive-query size bounds under functional dependencies to classical information theory, says multiple constraint families can require infinitely many linear inequalities in an optimization formulation, and presents a quantum-information reformulation while noting practical-tightness challenges.
source_lineage.limitations: Only source metadata and abstract text were consumed in this bounded run; no full-text theorem verification was performed.

source_lineage.source: Abo Khamis, Nakos, Olteanu, and Suciu, Join Size Bounds using Lp-Norms on Degree Sequences
source_lineage.outcome: The abstract states that information-inequality upper bounds can incorporate relation sizes and max-degrees, and extends them with l_p norms of degree sequences, with computability and tightness claims under stated simple-degree conditions.
source_lineage.limitations: Only source metadata and abstract text were consumed; theorem hypotheses and proof details were not independently checked.

mapping: Represent a finite multi-set/intersection or nested symbolic constraint problem as a conjunctive-query/join hypergraph whose attributes are latent symbols and whose relation predicates encode admissible tuples.
Map partial observations to cardinality, marginal, degree, l_p-degree, or functional-dependency constraints on projections/relations.
Use entropy/polymatroid variables over attribute subsets to turn those observations into a convex/linear outer-bound program for log output cardinality.

Treat Shannon/submodular constraints as a computable outer relaxation; additional non-Shannon information inequalities form a principled tightening hierarchy when the outer relaxation is not known complete.
bounded_synthesis.connection_value: This supplies a reusable certification architecture for the project: every reported cardinality upper bound can carry both a numerical certificate and a completeness label tied to the inequality family used. The distinction between the entropic region and tractable polymatroid/Shannon outer relaxations naturally expresses a failure/completeness boundary under partial observability rather than hiding it as estimator error.

proposed_toolkit_abstraction.constraint_compiler: symbolic predicates/nesting -> query hypergraph plus projection/dependency constraints
proposed_toolkit_abstraction.bound_engine: maximize target joint entropy/log-cardinality over a chosen inequality cone
proposed_toolkit_abstraction.certificate: return upper bound, inequality family, source observations used, and whether tightness is proved, conditionally proved, or only outer-relaxation certified
proposed_toolkit_abstraction.refinement_rule: If the Shannon/polymatroid relaxation is suspected loose, add source-qualified non-Shannon inequalities or stronger entropic constraints instead of silently treating the first LP as complete.

reliable: Conjunctive-query join cardinality and the target finite-constraint cardinality problem share a direct structural encoding through relations/hypergraphs.
Information-inequality methods support rigorous upper-bound formulations using relation cardinalities and degree-style observations.
A hierarchy from tractable polymatroid/Shannon relaxations toward stronger entropic constraints is a useful way to expose incompleteness explicitly.
uncertain: The exact smallest nested symbolic example exhibiting a strict Shannon-versus-entropic gap was not established in this slice.
The 2026 Zhang-Yeung-query details are supported only by a secondary search snippet in this run and require direct-source verification before theorem-level use.
